I don't think you should be depressed about it. In fact you should be glad that you are sensible enough to walk away from people who can't see that there can be two sides to most debates. I find especially on the internet, where people are anonymous, they will hold on to even the weakest argument. When they can't back up what they are saying they will move to name calling or site some clearly biased website or a YouTube video of some wacko with 200 subscribers.

You will find it is easy to recognize deadend conversations quickly if you know the signs.If they drop six or seven links to back up their point, and not one is from an organization you have heard of. Granted this is if you know what you are talking about. If you are discussing motorcycle repair and you know nothing about it, then you probably won't recognize sources by name, and you probably shouldn't be debating motor cycle repair. The biggest sign of an unbending know-it-all is that they speak in absolutes. "Everybody from Kentucky is an illiterate hillbilly" or " everybody from Russia hates americans." Outside of mathematics and physics there are very few absolutes in the world. There are many things we hold to be true( the sun will rise in the morning and set at night), but that is based on history, not on any scientific data that guarantees it to be absolute. Between technological advances, evolution and the trillions and trillions of square miles of unknowns floating around in the universe, nearly nothing can be guaranteed over a long enough timeline.

So no I never "give up" on an argument, I just come to the realization that I have nothing to gain from debating closed minded individuals.And I don't get upset, I just picture that person as someone who is meek and ineffectual in real life and needs to fight tooth and nail on the internet because it is probably the only time in there life when they can feel like a winner. It's hard to be angry at sad people. Just walk away with a smile and let them feel like they won, it's kind of like letting your little brother beat you at basketball, he feels good and has no clue that he couldn't really beat you on his best day and your worst.
